answer: Forget the fable that one good puzzle filters farms: a solver is written once and copied. Instead, match each identity live, at an unpredictable minute, with a random peer from a distant cluster, for a short joint task whose prompts that peer invents on the spot. Standing grows only from signed transcripts spanning many unrelated clusters; clones mostly draw each other, forming a closed sable-dark component with no outside edges, and running many at once means many simultaneous divergent conversations one operator cannot staff. Nectar rewards thus follow external connection, not headcount.
